title: The Pentagon Hopes to Speed Up 'Kill Chain' AI Buys With 5-Minute Videos
key_facts: The Tradewinds program, run by the Pentagon's Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office (CDAO), lets companies submit videos of up to five minutes describing AI products for 'strategic focus areas'.
Accepted companies join the Tradewinds Solutions Marketplace and get 'post-competitive' status, which can help government buyers skip competition requirements and cut months from awards.
A DOD official says that in several instances the department made awards through Tradewinds in less than a week.
The 2026 topics include AI that can 'enhance force lethality' and AI agents that can assist the joint targeting process, including 'kill chain execution'.
Such deals are often 'other transaction' agreements, which avoid some federal acquisition rules; the Pentagon can spend up to $500 million on one without notifying Congress.

OpenAI, Anthropic and Google are listed as Tradewinds participants; public records show all three have other transaction deals with the CDAO, but the companies did not confirm Tradewinds was used for them.
Senator Joni Ernst of Iowa says the agreements raise red flags, including questionable costs, mishandled restricted information and weak oversight.
quote_evidence: "While OTAs offer opportunities to attract new procurement partners and reduce red tape, numerous reviews have raised red flags," US senator Joni Ernst of Iowa tells WIRED.
If accepted, the pitched products are considered "post-competitive."
why_it_matters_hint: Faster military buying of AI with less competition and less public spending data.
